papers.title: Optimizing aprocitentan dosing in elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension: a PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm modeling study.
papers.abstract: Aprocitentan is a dual endothelin receptor antagonist for resistant hypertension (RH), but its optimal use in elderly Chinese patients remains unclear. This study aimed to develop an integrated physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK)/pharmacodynamic (PD)-circadian rhythm model to suggest precision dosing and administration-time optimization in this special population. A PBPK model was developed using published clinical pharmacokinetic data and linked to a direct-effect sigmoid maximal effect model. Circadian blood pressure (BP) variation was described by a triple-harmonic cosine function. After validation against independent pharmacokinetic (PK) and PD datasets, the model was extrapolated to elderly Chinese patients by incorporating age-related physiology, uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 activity variability, and mild hepatic impairment. Sensitivity analyses and simulations were performed to evaluate exposure, BP response, and dosing time. The model showed acceptable predictive performance. Sensitivity analyses indicated that aprocitentan exposure was mainly influenced by ionization-, binding-, and distribution-related parameters. Plasma unbound fraction and liver volume were the major determinants of cumulative and steady-state area under the curve (AUC), while lipophilicity predominantly affected early exposure, mean residence time, and terminal half-life. Compared with healthy elderly Caucasian subjects, simulated steady-state AUC increased by 20.6% in elderly Chinese patients and by 52.5% in those with mild hepatic impairment. Among the simulated regimens, 6.25 mg once daily provided the most balanced exposure profile and maintained AUC and maximum plasma concentration within the prespecified reference range in both populations. The model identified 12:00-13:00 as an alternative administration window associated with a favorable simulated 24-hour BP profile. Under the model-predicted regimen, simulated reductions in systolic BP/diastolic BP were 13.04/8.97 mmHg in elderly Chinese RH patients and 13.63/9.37 mmHg in those with mild hepatic impairment, with 24-hour BP remaining mainly within the Grade 1 hypertension range. This study established an integrated PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm model for aprocitentan in elderly Chinese patients with RH. The simulations identified 6.25 mg once daily and midday administration as candidate strategies for further clinical evaluation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective PK/PD, ambulatory BP, safety, adherence, and clinical validation before implementation in clinical practice.

papers.title: A study on the temporal network characteristics of early post-chemotherapy core symptoms in colorectal cancer patients based on ecological momentary assessment.
papers.abstract: Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) often experience multiple concurrent symptoms during the early post-chemotherapy period, and both symptom severity and inter-symptom associations may change over time. Previous low-frequency assessments may not adequately capture short-term fluctuations. To characterize the dynamic trajectories and network features of early symptoms in patients receiving postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for CRC and to identify candidate symptoms for enhanced monitoring. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) was performed three times daily for seven consecutive days after infusion in the first and second chemotherapy cycles and covered 13 symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models characterized symptom trajectories, and a multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) model estimated temporal and contemporaneous networks. Edge uncertainty, centrality stability, sensitivity analyses, and between-cycle differences were evaluated. A total of 110 patients contributed 4,134 valid assessments (completion rate, 89.5%). All 13 symptoms showed significant time effects. Fatigue, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sleep disturbance fluctuated, whereas numbness/tingling and depression showed cumulative trends. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea had comparatively high outgoing temporal associations. The strongest individual temporal edge was modest (standardized coefficient approximately 0.12). No statistically significant between-cycle differences were found in overall network structure or global strength. Early post-chemotherapy symptoms showed dynamic changes and a broadly comparable network structure across the first two cycles. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea may be candidates for enhanced monitoring and future intervention research; the observational findings do not establish causal effects or intervention efficacy.

papers.title: [Clinical factors associated with recurrent vertigo of childhood and vestibular migraine of childhood and development of diagnostic prediction models].
papers.abstract: Objective: To characterize the clinical features of recurrent vertigo of childhood (RVC) and vestibular migraine of childhood (VMC), to identify factors independently associated with the diagnostic classification of RVC and VMC versus other causes of pediatric vertigo, and to develop and validate clinical diagnostic prediction models to facilitate the clinical recognition and differential diagnosis of pediatric vertigo. Methods: This retrospective study included 446 pediatric patients with vertigo who met the inclusion criteria and were treated at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients, who were classified according to the underlying etiology, and clinical characteristics, including age, sex, family history, and ancillary examination findings, were compared across etiologic groups. Separate binary classification analyses were performed for RVC versus non-RVC and VMC versus non-VMC. For the RVC analysis, all 446 patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=312) and a validation set (n=134) at a 7∶3 ratio; for the VMC analysis, 49 patients with probable vestibular migraine of childhood (PVMC) were excluded, leaving 397 patients who were randomly divided at the same ratio into a training set (n=278) and a validation set (n=119). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 29.0 and R version 4.3.2. Between-group comparisons were conducted using the χ² test or rank-sum test, as appropriate. In the training set, univariate analyses followed by multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with the diagnostic classification of VMC versus non-VMC and RVC versus non-RVC (P<0.05 was considered statistically significant). Nomogram-based diagnostic prediction models were subsequently developed and evaluated using calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results: Among the 446 children with vertigo, significant differences were observed among etiological groups in age, family history of migraine, electroencephalography, head MRI, hearing assessment, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels (P<0.05), whereas, no significant differences were observed in sex or other types of family history (P>0.05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified age, family history of migraine, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level as factors independently associated with VMC versus non-VMC classification. Compared with preschool-aged children (≤6 years), school-aged children (7-12 years; OR=9.50, 95%CI: 2.18-41.40) and adolescents (≥13 years; OR=16.03, 95%CI: 3.22-79.76) were positively associated with VMC classification. A family history of migraine was also positively associated with VMC classification (OR=4.20, 95%CI: 1.90-9.26), whereas, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level was negatively associated with VMC classification (OR=0.92, 95%CI: 0.88-0.97) (all P<0.05). Age, headache, electroencephalographic findings, brain MRI findings, and thyroid function were independently associated with RVC versus non-RVC classification. Compared with preschool-aged children, school-aged children (OR=0.18, 95%CI: 0.09-0.36) and adolescents (OR=0.03, 95%CI: 0-0.24) were negatively associated with RVC classification. Headache (OR=0.11, 95%CI: 0.05-0.26), abnormal electroencephalographic findings (OR=0.15, 95%CI: 0.06-0.42), and abnormal brain MRI findings (OR=0.33, 95%CI: 0.17-0.62) were also negatively associated with RVC classification, whereas, abnormal thyroid function was positively associated with RVC classification (OR=2.16, 95%CI: 1.06-4.40) (all P<0.05). Diagnostic prediction models for RVC and VMC were developed based on these independently associated factors. The areas under the ROC curve (AUC) for the RVC model was 0.86 and 0.85 in the training and validation sets, respectively, whereas, those for the VMC model were 0.80 and 0.74, respectively. Together with the calibration and DCA results, these findings indicated good diagnostic predictive performance of the models. Conclusions: Pediatric vertigo has heterogeneous etiologies and diverse clinical presentations. Age, headache, electroencephalographic findings, brain MRI findings, and thyroid function are independently associated with RVC classification, whereas age, family history of migraine, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level are independently associated with VMC classification, with lower serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels being more strongly associated with VMC. Diagnostic prediction models incorporating these clinical features demonstrate good discriminative performance, which may facilitate the clinical recognition and differential diagnosis of RVC and VMC in children.

papers.title: Association Between Cytomegalovirus and Fibromyalgia: A Large-Scale Retrospective Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia is a chronic widespread pain disorder with incompletely understood pathogenesis. Viral infections have been proposed as potential triggers, but studies examining cytomegalovirus (CMV), a herpesvirus establishing lifelong latency, and fibromyalgia are scarce. We investigated the association between CMV infection and subsequent fibromyalgia. This retrospective matched case-control study used a database of over 370,000 individuals from 01/2003 to 12/2025. Cases were defined by at least two fibromyalgia diagnoses separated by ≥ 6 months. Up to five controls per case were matched on year of birth, sex, lookback period, and neighborhood socioeconomic status. Exposure was defined as a positive CMV IgM or IgG test, with a two-year washout period. Conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios adjusted for psychiatric disorders, sleep disorders, obesity, and smoking. After exclusions, 1,811 cases were matched to 8,988 controls. Prior CMV exposure was documented in 50.7% of cases versus 45.6% of controls (P < 0.001). CMV infection was significantly associated with fibromyalgia (adjusted odds ratio 1.321; 95% CI 1.173-1.488; P < 0.001). The association persisted across stricter case definitions and alternative washout periods. CMV infection is significantly associated with increased odds of fibromyalgia. Prospective studies are warranted to establish causality and underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: The temporal representation of computational features from body expressions.
papers.abstract: Body expression is an important channel for human communication. To understand the underlying perceptual mechanisms, the present study used electroencephalography and time-resolved multivariate analyses to track the temporal emergence of computationally defined body features and their contribution to emotion representations. Six body postural features (i.e., limb angles, symmetry, shoulder ratio, surface, potential energy, and limb contraction) were computed based on fourteen body joints. Representational similarity analysis revealed that the body surface and potential energy were significantly encoded at an early stage, persisting for an extended duration over parietal- posterior electrodes. In contrast, limb contraction was encoded at a later stage and exhibited a shorter duration. Furthermore, commonality analysis demonstrated that the postural features of surface and potential energy explained the neural variance of emotion categories, with body surface accounting for the largest proportion of the shared neural variance. These findings provide empirical evidence for the temporal dynamics of computationally defined body-posture representations during emotional body perception and may inform future computational models of body expression perception.

papers.title: [Modifiable risk factors and diabetic retinopathy: a Mendelian randomization analysis].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the causal relationships of body mass index (BMI), smoking, alcohol and coffee consumption, sleep, physical activity, and educational attainment with diabetic retinopathy (DR) and its subtypes. Methods: We conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study. Genetic instruments were selected from seven large-scale European-descent genome-wide association studies. Summary-level statistics for three DR phenotypes were obtained from the FinnGen consortium. The inverse-variance weighted method was used as the main MR analysis, with weighted median, MR-Egger regression, maximum likelihood, and MR-PRESSO models used for sensitivity analyses to assess the robustness of the findings. The MR study was conducted from September to November 2024. Results: A total of 14 584 patients with DR and 202 082 control participants were included. For analyses of DR subtypes, 2 026 patients with non-proliferative DR and 204 208 control participants, as well as 8 681 patients with proliferative DR and 204 208 control participants, were included. Higher genetically predicted BMI was intensively and independently associated with increased risk of DR and subtypes. The odds ratio (OR) was 1.26 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.16-1.37, P<0.001] of overall DR, 1.68 (95%CI, 1.38-2.06, P<0.001) of non-proliferative DR, and 1.41 (95%CI, 1.27-1.56, P<0.001) of proliferative DR for 1-SD increase in BMI. Increased coffee consumption was associated with a higher risk of overall DR (OR=1.23; 95%CI, 1.04-1.45, P=0.015), non-proliferative DR (OR=1.72; 95%CI, 1.17-2.53, P=0.006), and proliferative DR (OR=1.33; 95%CI, 1.08-1.63, P=0.007). In addition, genetically predicted educational attainment was inversely associated with non-proliferative DR (OR=0.70; 95%CI, 0.55-0.90, P=0.005). Insufficient evidence was found to support the causal association of smoking, alcohol consumption, sleep, and physical activity with DR (all P>0.05). Conclusions: Based on MR analysis of European populations, higher BMI, increased coffee intake, and lower educational attainment are risk factors for DR.

papers.title: [Expert consensus on light therapy for the treatment of insomnia disorder (2026 edition)].
papers.abstract: Insomnia disorder is a common sleep disorder characterized by a high prevalence and a tendency toward chronicity, which may significantly affect patients' daytime functioning and quality of life. As a non-pharmacological physical intervention, light therapy may improve certain insomnia symptoms by modulating circadian phase and alertness, and has shown potential clinical value in patients with insomnia disorder, including those with circadian rhythm disturbances and selected comorbidities. However, existing studies remain limited by small sample sizes, substantial heterogeneity among study populations, inconsistent intervention parameters, and relatively short follow-up periods. Standardized application across different populations and clinical settings still lacks unified guidance. Based on this, the Chinese Sleep Research Society, the Sleep Disorders Rehabilitation Professional Committee of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine, and the Community and Primary Care Working Committee of Chinese Sleep Research Society, jointly organized a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop the Expert consensus on light therapy for the treatment of insomnia disorder (2026 edition). The consensus was developed based on the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. It systematically summarizes the mechanisms of action, clinical indications, treatment parameters, efficacy assessment, combination therapy, contraindications, and management of adverse events related to light therapy, and provides corresponding recommendations for special populations, including pregnant and postpartum women, elderly people, and adolescents. A total of 27 recommendations were formulated to provide systematic, standardized evidence-based guidance for the clinical application of light therapy in the treatment of insomnia disorder.
